extracted.intended_audience: Applicants preparing an NIH PHS 398 K08 Career Development (mentored) award; early-stage surgeon-scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and documenting a resubmission for an NIH PHS 398 K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Career Development Award, including required form sections, candidate career-development plan, mentor plans, vertebrate animal and human-subject/biomaterial disclosures, budget justification, and benchmarks for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form - Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists required sections for the PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form: Introduction (for Resubmission and Revision applications); Candidate Section; Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development; Research Plan Section (Specific Aims; Research Strategy); Progress Report Publication List (for Renewal applications); Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Other Candidate Information Section (Candidate's Plan to Provide Mentoring); Mentor, Co-Mentor, Consultant, Collaborators Section (Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s); Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants); Environment and Institutional Commitment to Candidate Section (Description of Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development; Description of Candidate's Contribution to Program Goals); Other Research Plan Section (Vertebrate Animals; Select Agent Research; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements); Resource Sharing; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed section must be included as part of the Career Development Award supplemental materials (examples show attached PDFs for Introduction, Candidate Section, Aims, Research Strategy, RCR training, mentor plan, institutional docs, vertebrate animals, resource sharing, authentication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Section - euthanasia and AVMA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are vertebrate animals euthanized? If 'Yes' — Is the method consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines? If 'No' to AVMA guidelines, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must explicitly answer the euthanasia question and, when applicable, state consistency with AVMA guidelines or provide justification for deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income Section - disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Is program income anticipated during the periods for which grant support is requested? If 'Yes', use the provided format to reflect anticipated amount(s) and source(s). If 'No', leave blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If program income is anticipated, provide Budget Period, Anticipated Amount ($), and Source(s) in the specified format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells Section - disclosure and registry citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? If 'Yes', list the registration number(s) of the specific cell line(s) from the NIH registry or check the box indicating that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a specific stem cell line cannot be referenced at submission, indicate that a line from the registry will be used and provide registration numbers when available; follow NIH stem cell registry guidance (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Fetal Tissue Section - compliance documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed project involve human fetal tissue obtained from elective abortions? If 'Yes' then provide the HFT Compliance Assurance and the HFT Sample IRB Consent Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, attach the required compliance assurance and sample IRB consent documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents Section (Renewal applications) - disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions and Patents: Indicate 'Yes' or 'No' for involvement. If 'Yes', indicate whether previously reported ('Previously Reported: Yes/No').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal applicants must disclose inventions/patents and prior reporting history in the specified fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Budget - required budget sections (A through K)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cumulative budget form must include Sections A (Senior/Key Person), B (Other Personnel), Total Number Other Personnel, Total Salary/Wages and Fringe Benefits (A+B), Section C Equipment, Section D Travel (1. Domestic; 2. Foreign), Section E Participant/Trainee Support Costs (tuition/fees/health insurance, stipends, travel, subsistence, other, number of participants), Section F Other Direct Costs (materials/supplies, publication costs, consultant services, ADP/computer services, subawards/consortium/contractual costs, equipment or facility rental/user fees, alterations/renovations, other 1-3), Section G Direct Costs (A thru F), Section H Indirect Costs, Section I Total Direct and Indirect Costs (G + H), Section J Fee, Section K Total Costs and Fee (I + J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals for each section and complete all required budget blocks per the Research & Related Budget format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification - personnel, fringe, supplies, services, equipment, travel, indirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify personnel effort and fringe benefits (example: 'The professional fringe benefit rate for Dr. Al-Adra is budgeted at 33.6% for the duration of the grant'). Provide line-item justification for supplies/other expenses (cell isolation/culture consumables; pre-operative/operative disposables; perfusion additives & consumables), core service fees (histology, flow cytometry at specified $/hour), equipment purchases (e.g., Nanosight Imaging Microscope), animal expenses (purchase, shipping, housing per diems), travel (conference registration, meals/hotel, flights), and Indirect Cost Rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimated quantities/hours, unit costs, and rationale for each item; cite core facility hourly rates and supply lists; state indirect cost rate (example: 8% per RFA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors (no salary requested) - mentor qualifications and mentoring roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe mentors' positions, research focus, prior funding history, and mentoring roles. Example language: Mentor will serve as primary mentor to the PI and guide overall direction of research and career development through weekly meetings; co-mentors will meet weekly/monthly to discuss specific aspects of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate mentors' extensive history of independent funding and mentoring success (list prior awards like K08, R01, R21, U01, U54, R35), explicitly state meeting frequency (weekly, monthly), and describe the mentoring activities (guide research direction, develop technical expertise, discuss immunological aspects, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Statement / Career Goals and Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the candidate's career objective (e.g., 'pursue and answer original research questions and become a recognized authority in Transplantation Immunology') and how the K08 will address gaps in education/training to develop an independent research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain prior background, specific training gaps, short-term and long-term goals, and how planned activities will lead to independence and future R01-level funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Career Development and Training Plan - core components
rubrics_metrics.description: The training plan should include: (1) Development of academic expertise in relevant fields (e.g., Transplantation Immunology, Dendritic Cell Biology, Biostatistics) via courses/conferences/journal clubs; (2) Regular meetings with the mentorship team to develop research vision and focus; (3) Laboratory training and experience to lead an independent research group (investigative techniques, research development, manuscript submission planning); (4) Professional development (leadership, management, research administration) and Responsible Conduct of Research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify courses (examples given: Advanced Course in Basic and Clinical Immunology; BMI 541; BMI 542), meeting schedules (weekly mentor meetings, semi-annual critical feedback meetings), training curricula (UW ICTR seminars, mentor training curricula), and concrete training activities and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training - documentation and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Enroll in an NIH-accepted RCR course (example: Pharmacy 800) that meets Office of Research Integrity requirements; discuss RCR with mentors during semi-annual meetings; mentors will ensure ongoing updates and be available to discuss ethical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include course name, schedule, affirm that it meets NIH requirements, and describe integration of RCR training into mentorship meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Benchmarks for Successful Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Define concrete benchmarks by end of award: generate a competitive R01 application; produce a target number of publications (example: 4 publications during the award); present and submit abstracts (example: average two per year); participate in a K-to-R grant writing workshop in Year 4; prepare and submit R01 in Years 4-5; engage in mentor training and leadership development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the R01 submission as the primary benchmark; describe intermediate outputs (publications, abstracts, presentations) and steps to achieve them (workshops, mentor feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Response Expectations (address reviewer criticisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: When resubmitting, explicitly respond to reviewer weaknesses by revising the career development plan, providing new preliminary data, optimizing technical approaches (e.g., collaborate with experienced microsurgeons), adding specificity (e.g., more specific assays to isolate DC effects), adding mechanistic experiments (e.g., DC expansion and depletion experiments, specifying methods to deplete PD-L1 and extracellular vesicles), adding early predetermined immunologic time points, expanding cytokine analyses, and including standardized histopathology criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a point-by-point introduction summarizing major conceptual and strategic revisions made in response to reviewer comments (example enumerates 7 specific areas of revision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Progression, Dissemination, and Networking Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for presenting data at scientific meetings (e.g., American Transplant Congress, Great Lakes Transplant Immunology Forum), submitting abstracts (~2/year), presenting at departmental research summits, preparing manuscripts (goal of multiple publications), and leveraging meetings for collaborations and future multi-PI grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify expected dissemination (abstracts/year, target journals), describe networking strategies and how presentations feed into future grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring Meeting Structure and Feedback Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish regular and specified meeting schedules: weekly meetings with primary mentor for directed discussions; weekly attendance of mentor's lab meetings; weekly or monthly meetings with co-mentors for technical and career advice; semi-annual two-way critical feedback meetings with mentor team to present training plan and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document meeting cadence and purposes (career development, technical training, manuscript/grant preparation), and include plans for semi-annual formal progress reviews with mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Core Facilities and Service Fees - justification and estimated usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify core services required (UW Histology core, UW Flow Cytometry core at specified hourly rates, Nanosight Imaging Microscope) and provide estimated hours/usage and reagent/antibody costs necessary to complete aims; include animal purchase/shipping/housing per diems and calculate per-animal or per-cage/day costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimated hours (examples: ~100 hours for some assays), per-hour costs (example: $65/hour for flow cytometry), number of animals, cages, and periods of housing; justify why each core/service is needed for the specific aims.
